question: Does fixed two-bin m_hhh profiling improve point-vs-point median Asimov separation relative to a single bin?
figure: 8 lower-left panel, red dashed and blue dotted
simulated_channel: bbb b gamma gamma (two H to bb and one H to gamma gamma), illustrative only, no detector efficiency map
cut_rule: twice the on-shell 3h threshold 3*125 GeV, selected before reading bin differences or executing the likelihood
axis_policy: integrate only the source histogram displayed window (preserve step widths and log-to-linear); no unmeasured overflow
comparison: Both truth directions; native LO rate ratio and exact equal total control. Independently normalized two-point shape; background and signal fraction nuisances preserve totals (Gaussian auxiliary constraints). Only interpret q_A as median Asimov discrimination proxy, not calibrated Z or CLs.
acceptance: Positive two-bin increment for both directions after profiling; identical shape negative control and one/two-bin data processing check; independent profile optimizer; explicitly assess plausibility, not claim ATLAS/CMS projection.
